title: 878. Super Egg Drop

examples.explanation: With one egg there is no room for risk, so both floors must be tried from the bottom up.
Three drops always suffice (for instance, first try floor 3), and two drops cannot cover 6 floors.
Four drops cover up to 4 + 6 + 4 = 14 floors with three eggs, and three drops fall short.

hints: Flip the question: with m drops and e eggs, the tallest tower you can resolve is dp[m][e] = dp[m-1][e-1] + dp[m-1][e] + 1.
Grow the drop count until the coverage reaches n; a one-dimensional table updated from high eggs to low eggs is enough.
